item.title: Alabama heads into a second primary election after redistricting
item.description: Alabama voters are again selecting candidates for four Congressional districts after the state changed the district map to favor Republicans. The redistricting is causing confusion among voters.
item.content:encoded: Alabama voters are again selecting candidates for four Congressional districts after the state changed the district map to favor Republicans. The redistricting is causing confusion among voters.

item.title: Ancient relics in Syria face new dangers after end of civil war
item.description: Syria has a rich archaeological heritage full of ancient Roman and Byzantine sites and treasures. Damaged and stolen during a civil war, they now face an increased danger of looting.
item.content:encoded: Syria has a rich archaeological heritage full of ancient Roman and Byzantine sites and treasures. Damaged and stolen during a civil war, they now face an increased danger of looting.

item.title: ICE crackdown in Minnesota changed the race for open U.S. Senate seat
item.description: President Trump's immigration crackdown in Minnesota earlier this year is a key issue going into that state's competitive Democratic primary for an open U.S. Senate seat.

item.title: Former U.S. diplomat on Iran's latest demands
item.description: NPR's Juana Summers speaks with Wendy Sherman, a former U.S. diplomat who has been part of teams negotiating with Iran, about the status of latest negotiations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

item.description: A whitewater rafting group brings people of different political persuasions together to talk and paddle.

item.title: Powerful Colombia quake kills at least 111, trapping dozens under collapsed buildings
item.description: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck Colombia toppling buildings and trapping people. Several dozen were reported dead.

item.title: Why is Texas Gov. Greg Abbott pausing permits to build new data centers?
item.description: Texas is on track to become the country's largest data center market. But the governor has effectively issued a pause on new centers until the state can audit their energy and water usage.

item.title: After his Reflecting Pool vandalism case is dismissed, David Hearn looks for closure
item.description: The ex-Olympian accused of damaging the reflecting pool tells NPR the experience has been "Orwellian" and "Kafkaesque." And it's not over yet: His lawyers are fighting to close the case permanently.

item.title: Who really needs testosterone?
item.description: The military plans to start screening service members for low testosterone, and social media is overflowing with over-the-top claims about low-T. But who actually needs testosterone therapy?

item.title: Why Monarch Butterflies are North America's insect mascot
item.description: Vann Newkirk, senior editor at The Atlantic, loves butterflies, especially monarch butterflies. He sat down with NPR's Juana Summers to dig into a trip to Mexico that helped him explore his passion.
